stories.title: General natural-key snapshot-sync path + SNAPSHOT_SYNC registry (Atlas-ruled, F-115-reusable)
acceptance: Pi SNAPSHOT_SYNC registry {table -> (naturalKeyCols, cursorCol)} + a snapshot reader that deltas by an explicit recorded_at cursor per table (tracked in sync_log) -- NOT full-snapshot, NOT rowid (TEXT-PK tables have no stable rowid; VACUUM renumbers)
server natural-key upsert parameterized by naturalKeyCols -> UNIQUE(source_device, *naturalKeyCols) + ON-CONFLICT; a NEW pattern, distinct from the id->source_id registry path
A-4 guard: each table's naturalKeyCols defined ONCE, referenced by both tiers (shared contract, not two drifting lists)
does NOT touch or refactor dtc_freeze_frame's FK-resolution special-case (leave shipped code alone)
unit tests: idempotent re-sync on the natural key; cursor bounds volume
ruff check passes

validationCriteria.action: register a test table in SNAPSHOT_SYNC and run two sync cycles
validationCriteria.outcome: server rows dedup on the natural key; re-sync is idempotent (no duplicates, no regression)
defined once in a shared contract referenced by both Pi and server (A-4), not two lists

stories.goal: As the system, I want a reusable table-parameterized snapshot-sync mechanism for TEXT-PK / insert-once tables, so startup_log (and F-115's event-vault) can sync without the integer-delta cursor.

pmSignOff.rationale: General reusable snapshot-sync mechanism (registry + Pi snapshot reader + parameterized server upsert + A-4 single-definition) is intrinsically one cohesive unit -- splitting the mechanism from itself would fragment the contract. Atlas-ruled shape. startup_log (US-417) is the separate consumer story. If Ralph compresses, flag and PM will split the server-upsert half out.

acceptance: VERIFY-FIRST: re-query the deployed Pi; prior backoff/cadence work (US-325/US-332) may have fixed some -- if a live table is healthy, close as already-fixed WITH EVIDENCE rather than changing code

validationCriteria.outcome: connection_log + sync_history idle growth is materially reduced OR closed-as-already-healthy with row-count evidence; real events still logged

stories.title: Pi post-reboot clock-drift guard (F-080, code angle; verify-first)
acceptance: VERIFY-FIRST: re-query the Pi (timedatectl, hwclock, systemctl status systemd-timesyncd, recent power_log timestamps); if the clock is sane post-reboot (fixed out-of-band), close as not-needed WITH EVIDENCE

if still drifting: the startup_log/power_log timestamp writers gain a boot-time sanity guard -- the first post-boot row's timestamp is validated against an NTP-confirmed/monotonic source; drift beyond threshold flags data_quality='clock_unsynced' rather than writing drifted time as truth
a unit test simulates a pre-NTP-sync boot timestamp and asserts the guard flags (not crashes)
the RTC coin-cell / timesyncd ordering fix is ops (AI-1), out of this story's scope
ruff check passes

validationCriteria.action: simulate a pre-NTP-sync boot timestamp through the writer

stories.goal: As the CIO, I want post-reboot log timestamps to be sane, so power/boot history is not corrupted by RTC drift.

stories.title: Foreign-vehicle contamination marker + ingest guard (F-116, Atlas-ruled)
acceptance: Marker 2 axes: data_source='foreign' added to the SSOT src/pi/obdii/data_source.py DATA_SOURCE_VALUES (propagates to all 5 Pi table CHECKs) + mirrored on the server data_source CHECK -- the PRIMARY row-level exclusion axis (every WHERE data_source='real' query auto-excludes it, zero consumer changes; NOT 'fixture' -- risks evidence deletion). AND data_quality='foreign_vehicle' added to src/server/analytics/drive_statistics_compute.py DRIVE_STATISTICS_DATA_QUALITY_VALUES SSOT + the model enum (the :101 divergence assertion stays green)
A-4: both forward-only CHECK migrations applied IDENTICALLY on both tiers (define once per SSOT, mirror the other -- not two hand-maintained lists)

re-tag drive 33: Spool runs the reclassification SQL once the enums land (realtime_data.data_source='foreign' + drive_summary.data_quality='foreign_vehicle' WHERE drive_id=33) -- re-tag, NEVER delete (evidence preserved)

ingest guard = sustained bus-rate check (primary): aggregate rate over a ROLLING WINDOW > ~7/s (Eclipse K-line ceiling ~6.3/s) -> flag foreign; SUSTAINED not instantaneous (no false-flag on a legit Eclipse burst); on trip -> flag/quarantine (mark foreign), NEVER silently delete. NOT a dongle-MAC allowlist (same dongle both vehicles), NOT VIN (Mode-09 silent -> backwards); protocol-ID deferred (no accessor today)

placement layered: Pi-side PRIMARY (on trip, retro-tag the open drive's rows foreign + do not sync as real; A-9-adjacent, do not couple) + server-side BACKSTOP tripwire like detect_overlapping_drives (resize-droppable if tight -- marker + Pi guard are the must-haves)
Rule-10: specs/architecture.md data-contract section names the foreign/foreign_vehicle values + the bus-rate guard, in-sprint
ruff check passes

validationCriteria.action: add the two enum values + run a query filtering WHERE data_source='real'
validationCriteria.outcome: foreign rows are auto-excluded with zero consumer changes; both CHECK migrations identical on both tiers (A-4)

validationCriteria.action: feed a sustained >7/s sample stream through the Pi guard
validationCriteria.outcome: the drive's rows are retro-tagged foreign and not synced as real; a legit Eclipse burst is NOT false-flagged
drive 33's 1,364 rows become data_source='foreign' + drive_summary foreign_vehicle; rows preserved, none deleted

stories.goal: As the CIO, I want foreign-vehicle rows honestly markable and prevented from recurring, so the Explorer (drive 33) cannot pollute real-data tuning queries.

pmSignOff.rationale: Atlas-ruled 4-part (2 marker-enum axes + re-tag + Pi bus-rate guard + server tripwire) but tightly coupled around one data-contract change. Server tripwire is Atlas-flagged RESIZE-DROPPABLE (marker + Pi guard are the must-haves) -- the built-in relief valve if it runs heavy. Build order: enums+re-tag first, then Pi guard, then server tripwire (drop if compressing).
